title: Paraformaldehyde Animal Perfusion for Fixed Tissue Extraction
author: Roberto Garcia Swinburn
materials: Stop the pump and remove needle.
Program the pump to start at 10 ml/min.

steps.title: Prepare Reagents and Equipment
steps.instruction: Prepare the necessary solutions and surgical tools for the procedure.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 50 ml Falcon tube with PBS1X and another with 4% PFA, maintaining both on ice.
Prepare surgical tools: blunt-end scissors, blunt forceps, small sharp-end scissors, and a surgical mouse silicon pad.
Prepare the surgical area with toxic waste disposal containers or PFA Neutralizing Absorbent Pads.

steps.title: Prepare Perfusion Pump and Needle
steps.instruction: Set up the pump and needle assembly to ensure it is primed and safe for injection.

substeps.instruction: Run water through the tube to clean it.
Create a needle stop at the bevel of the 27G butterfly needle (e.g., by cutting the needle cover up to the bevel) to prevent piercing the cardiac walls.
Install the needle on the pump tube.
Run PBS1X through the tube until it is filled and ready for use.
Ensure the 27G butterfly needle contains ice-cold PBS1X.

steps.title: Anesthetize the Animal
steps.instruction: Induce and maintain deep anesthesia to ensure a narcotic overdose.

substeps.instruction: Induce anesthesia using isoflurane-soaked tissue inside a 50 ml Falcon tube by placing the mouse's head inside until movement stops and breathing slows.
Inject 100 mg/kg pentobarbital IP (alternatively, use 100 mg/kg ketamine).
Verify terminal anesthesia by confirming the lack of pedal reflex (no paw retraction when pinched).

steps.title: Position and Secure the Animal
steps.instruction: Secure the mouse on the surgical surface.

substeps.instruction: Place the animal on the surgery pad with limbs positioned away from the chest.
Secure the animal using surgical tape on a PFA neutralizing pad placed on top of the silicon surgical pad (or use needles to pin the animal).

steps.title: Expose the Heart
steps.instruction: Surgically expose the thoracic cavity to access the heart.

substeps.instruction: Use blunt-end scissors and blunt forceps to cut the skin and muscular fascia of the lower abdomen, below the rib cage, to expose the liver and diaphragm.
Carefully move the livers to access the diaphragm and ribs.
Cut the diaphragm and the ribs by the sides using scissors, taking care not to cut the heart or lungs.

steps.title: Perform PBS1X Perfusion
steps.instruction: Flush the circulatory system with PBS1X to exsanguinate the animal.

substeps.instruction: Cut the right atrium of the heart with small sharp scissors to allow the injected volume to escape.
Inject the PBS1X needle into the left ventricle.
Start the pump at 10 ml/min (e.g., using an Agnthos' Peristaltic Pump 120U at 25 rpm; verify rpm for 10 ml/min flow rate).
Exsanguinate the animal with 50 ml PBS1X until the liver turns from red to a yellowish-fleshy color.
Switch the perfusion fluid to 50 ml of 4% PFA (specifically: Formaldehyde 4% stabilised, buffered pH 7.0 ±0.1, VWR Chemicals #9713).
Continue perfusion until muscles begin to fix.

steps.title: Post-Procedure Cleanup
steps.instruction: Clean the equipment or prepare for the next animal.

substeps.instruction: If continuing with another animal, rinse the tube with water and refill with PBS1X.
Otherwise, clean and discard waste according to local policies.
